c101: Mainly close-up dog faces and furry dog bodies (boxer face, small tan dog, dark shaggy dog). Others: warm orange/brown textured surfaces and objects (striped shell, wood furniture, peeling red paint, ceramic mug, cloth), plus people in mid-distance. Centre is often a face or orange-brown surface.
k163: Close-up of the face of a dog (mostly black-and-white or brown-and-white, especially snout, nose and eyes), filling the frame. Other kinds: a skunk face, and small dark rounded objects such as an oil filter, camera lens, glass cup rim, a green beetle, a cucumber.
k23: Close-up of high-contrast, finely patterned or ornate surfaces: orange-and-black butterfly wings with white-dotted edges, keyboard keys, spoked wheels and rims, skull or floral prints, spotted animal fur, dog eyes. Mostly sharp, regular, repeating small details filling the frame; a few other objects (helmet face, dragonfly, fire truck).
k275: Close-up of a round eye (pupil and iris) of an animal, mostly primates, dogs and frogs, seen from very near. Other kinds: round dark circular parts of objects, such as a gas-mask filter, a tractor wheel hub, a machine knob or a disc end, and sunglasses lenses.
k297: Mainly the face, neck and upper torso of a person (a smiling mouth and chin, a shirt collar, a mid-chest shirt) seen at medium close range, often outdoors. Also a few animals at the centre: a dog's head, a kudu body, a gas-mask face.
k305: Close-up of animal faces, mainly the nose and muzzle of dogs (black, white, tan noses, often with mouth or tongue), centred on the nose. Others: bird eye and beak (hawk, speckled bird), a snake on an arm, bare skin and limbs, a bow tie, small phone parts.
k97: Mixed close-ups of a single object filling the centre: mostly smooth rounded containers (pill bottle, flowered mug, metal percolator, jar with lid), then animal heads and paws, fur, a toy jet, a doll face, burnt matchsticks, a fish held in hands. Medium to close view.
p: Close-up faces of long-furred dogs (snout, nose, mouth, eye, often with tongue out), face-centred and close or medium view. Fewer cases: eyes or faces of other furry animals (meerkat, primate), and one human face and a wall clock.
